# DATA {data-background="slide_background.svg"}

Here we load the small simulated data set. For this case $p=3$.

We remove the first column of each matrix as it contains the indexes.

```{r data_load, echo=F, results='hide',  cache=F}
library(tidyr)
G_ = read.csv(file = "../data/example_data_G.csv",header=TRUE)
F_ = read.csv(file = "../data/example_data_F.csv",header=TRUE)
E_ = read.csv(file = "../data/example_data_E.csv", header=TRUE)
X_ = read.csv(file = "../data/example_data_X.csv", header=TRUE)

N <- nrow(G_[,-1])
M <- ncol(X_[,-1])
P <- ncol(G_[,-1])
t <- G_[,1]
t <- (t - t[1])/(1e9)/3600
t<- diff(t)
X_ <- X_[,-1]
E_ <- E_[,-1]
F_ <- F_[,-1]
G_ <- G_[,-1]
F_ <- apply(F_, MARGIN=2, FUN = as.numeric)
par(mfrow=c(2,3))
plot(G_[,1], type="l")
plot(G_[,2], type="l")
plot(G_[,3], type="l")
plot(F_[1,], type="l")
plot(F_[2,], type="l")
plot(F_[3,], type="l")
 
```

## Data characterisation {data-background="slide_background.svg"}

We run a simple analysis on the data using the PCA, we use mean imputation in case of missing data.

```{r pca, echo=F,  cache=F}
library(ggfortify)
imputed_ts_data <- apply(X_, MARGIN = 2, \(x){
  y=x
  y[is.na(x)]=mean(x,na.rm=TRUE)
  y
  } )
pca <- prcomp(imputed_ts_data, scale. = TRUE)
autoplot(pca)
```

## Varimax rotation {data-background="slide_background.svg"}

A simple and quick way to do source separation is to use the Varimax rotations over the PCA

```{r varimax, echo=F, message=F, warning=F, results='hide'}
library(vsp)
fa <- imputed_ts_data %>% as.matrix() %>% vsp( rank = 3)
plot_varimax_z_pairs(fa)
```

We observe weak to moderate anticorrelation between the inferred axes.

Now we correlate with the original simulated G factors

```{r corplot, echo=F}
library(corrplot)
corrplot(cor(G_, as.matrix(fa$Z), use = "pairwise.complete.obs"))
```

```{r lines, echo = FALSE}
par(mfrow=c(1,3))
plot(G_[,1],as.matrix(fa$Z)[,1])
plot(G_[,2],as.matrix(fa$Z)[,2])
plot(G_[,3],as.matrix(fa$Z)[,3])
 
```

### Conclusions {data-background="slide_background.svg"}

The sources should be well separated in this dataset.

## BAMF {data-background="slide_background.svg"}

Here is the original BAMF model:

```{stan output.var='priors', eval = FALSE, tidy = FALSE}
functions {
  matrix vector_array_to_matrix(vector[] x) {
    matrix[size(x), rows(x[1])] y;
    for (m in 1:size(x))
      y[m] = x[m]';
    return y;
  }
}

data {
  int<lower=1> n;     // number of data points
  int<lower=1> m;     // number of dimensions
  int<lower=1> p;     // number of components
  matrix[n,m] X;      // data matrix
  matrix<lower=0>[n,m] sigma;  // separate sigma for each of the observations (!)
  vector<lower=0>[n-1] timesteps; //How much time elapses between values in X (arbitrary unit, but unit choice also affects other priors)
  real<lower=0> minerr; //Minimal error
}

transformed data {
  vector[n*m] Xv = to_vector(X);
  vector[n*m] sigmav = to_vector(sigma);
}

parameters {
  matrix<lower=0>[n,p] G; // score matrix
  simplex[m] F[p]; // loadings simplex
  vector<lower=0>[p] alpha_a; // Posterior a
  vector<lower=minerr>[p] alpha_b; // Posterior b
}

model {

  // The priors for G and F are implicitly given in the parameters section,
  //  so explicitly stating them here would only lead to unnecessary calculations
  //  (uniform priors become additive constants (in logspace), that can be ignored).
  
  // Column-wise autocorrelation
  for(j in 1:p) {
    G[2:,j] ~ cauchy(G[:(n-1),j], alpha_a[j]*timesteps + alpha_b[j]);
  }

  // X ~ Z = G * F
  Xv ~ normal(to_vector(G*vector_array_to_matrix(F)), sigmav);

}
```

We use cmdstan to compile and run the different models.

```{r, results="hide"}
library(cmdstanr)
set_cmdstan_path("~/cmdstan")
file = "../models/bamf.stan"

mod <- cmdstan_model(file)
data_list <- list(n=N, m=M , p=P, X=X_, sigma=E_, timesteps=t, minerr=
    min((E_)) / 10
)
```

## Original BAMF model {data-background="slide_background.svg"}

```{r, results='hide', message=F, echo=F,warning=F}

fit_bamf <- mod$sample(
  data = data_list, 
  seed = 123, 
  chains = 4, 
  parallel_chains = 4,
  refresh = 0 # print update every 500 iters
)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, results='hide'}
library(posterior)
fit_bamf$diagnostic_summary()
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, results='hide'}
library(bayesplot)
fit_bamf$cmdstan_diagnose()
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, results='hide'}
mcmc_rhat(rhat(fit_bamf))
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, results='hide'}
mcmc_neff(neff_ratio(fit_bamf))
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, results='hide'}
draws <- fit_bamf$draws(format="df")
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, results='hide'}
library(tidyverse)
G_1 <- as_tibble(draws) %>% select( matches('G\\[\\d+,1'))
G_2 <- as_tibble(draws) %>% select( matches('G\\[\\d+,2'))
G_3 <- as_tibble(draws) %>% select( matches('G\\[\\d+,3'))
F_1 <- as_tibble(draws) %>% select( matches('F\\[1,\\d'))
F_2 <- as_tibble(draws) %>% select( matches('F\\[2,\\d'))
F_3 <- as_tibble(draws) %>% select( matches('F\\[3,\\d'))
```

let's plot the mean over posterior samples

```{r, echo=FALSE, results='hide'}
G1_mean <- G_1 %>% colMeans()
G2_mean <- G_2 %>% colMeans()
G3_mean <- G_3 %>% colMeans()
F1_mean <- F_1 %>% colMeans()
F2_mean <- F_2 %>% colMeans()
F3_mean <- F_3 %>% colMeans()
G1_sd <- G_1 %>% as.matrix() %>% matrixStats::colSds()
G2_sd <- G_2 %>% as.matrix() %>% matrixStats::colSds()
G3_sd <- G_3 %>% as.matrix() %>% matrixStats::colSds()
F1_sd <- F_1 %>% as.matrix() %>% matrixStats::colSds()
F2_sd <- F_2 %>% as.matrix() %>% matrixStats::colSds()
F3_sd <- F_3 %>% as.matrix() %>% matrixStats::colSds()
par(mfrow=c(2,3)) 
plot(G1_mean, type ="l")
plot(G2_mean, type ="l")
plot(G3_mean, type ="l")
plot(F1_mean, type ="l")
plot(F2_mean, type ="l")
plot(F3_mean, type ="l")
 
```

Here we plot the correlation between the posterior means and the original G values

```{r, echo=FALSE, results='hide'}
corrplot(cor(cbind(G1_mean,G2_mean,G3_mean),G_))
```

Here we plot the posterior means vs the original values of G and F

```{r, echo=FALSE, results='hide'}
par(mfrow=c(2,3))
plot(G_[,1],G1_mean)
plot(G_[,2],G2_mean)
plot(G_[,3],G3_mean)
plot(F_[1,],F1_mean)
plot(F_[2,],F2_mean)
plot(F_[3,],F3_mean)
```

Here we plot the z-scores for G and F, everything should be between 2 and -2 (95% confidence interval)

```{r, echo=FALSE, results='hide'}
par(mfrow=c(2,3))
plot((G_[,1]-G1_mean)/G1_sd, main="z-scores")
abline(h=2)
abline(h=-2)
plot((G_[,2]-G2_mean)/G2_sd)
abline(h=2)
abline(h=-2)
plot((G_[,3]-G3_mean)/G3_sd)
abline(h=2)
abline(h=-2)
plot((F_[1,]-F1_mean)/F1_sd)
abline(h=2)
abline(h=-2)
plot((F_[2,]-F2_mean)/F2_sd)
abline(h=2)
abline(h=-2)
plot((F_[3,]-F3_mean)/F3_sd)
abline(h=2)
abline(h=-2)
```

Let's define some functions to carry the above diagnostics

```{r, echo=FALSE, results='hide'}
quick_diagnostic_plots <- function(stan_fit){
  stan_fit$diagnostic_summary()
  stan_fit$cmdstan_diagnose()
  mcmc_rhat(rhat(fit_bamf))
  mcmc_neff(neff_ratio(fit_bamf))
  draws <- stan_fit$draws(format="df")
  G_1 <- as_tibble(draws) %>% select( matches('G\\[\\d+,1'))
  G_2 <- as_tibble(draws) %>% select( matches('G\\[\\d+,2'))
  G_3 <- as_tibble(draws) %>% select( matches('G\\[\\d+,3'))
  F_1 <- as_tibble(draws) %>% select( matches('F\\[1,\\d'))
  F_2 <- as_tibble(draws) %>% select( matches('F\\[2,\\d'))
  F_3 <- as_tibble(draws) %>% select( matches('F\\[3,\\d'))
  G1_mean <- G_1 %>% colMeans()
  G2_mean <- G_2 %>% colMeans()
  G3_mean <- G_3 %>% colMeans()
  F1_mean <- F_1 %>% colMeans()
  F2_mean <- F_2 %>% colMeans()
  F3_mean <- F_3 %>% colMeans()
  G1_sd <- G_1 %>% as.matrix() %>% matrixStats::colSds()
  G2_sd <- G_2 %>% as.matrix() %>% matrixStats::colSds()
  G3_sd <- G_3 %>% as.matrix() %>% matrixStats::colSds()
  F1_sd <- F_1 %>% as.matrix() %>% matrixStats::colSds()
  F2_sd <- F_2 %>% as.matrix() %>% matrixStats::colSds()
  F3_sd <- F_3 %>% as.matrix() %>% matrixStats::colSds()
  par(mfrow=c(2,3)) 
  plot(G1_mean, type ="l")
  plot(G2_mean, type ="l")
  plot(G3_mean, type ="l")
  plot(F1_mean, type ="l")
  plot(F2_mean, type ="l")
  plot(F3_mean, type ="l")
   
  corrplot(cor(cbind(G1_mean,G2_mean,G3_mean),G_))
   
  par(mfrow=c(2,3))
  plot(G_[,1],G1_mean)
  plot(G_[,2],G2_mean)
  plot(G_[,3],G3_mean)
  plot(F_[1,],F1_mean)
  plot(F_[2,],F2_mean)
  plot(F_[3,],F3_mean)
   
  par(mfrow=c(2,3))
  plot((G_[,1]-G1_mean)/G1_sd)
  abline(h=2)
  abline(h=-2)
  plot((G_[,2]-G2_mean)/G2_sd)
  abline(h=2)
  abline(h=-2)
  plot((G_[,3]-G3_mean)/G3_sd)
  abline(h=2)
  abline(h=-2)
  plot((F_[1,]-F1_mean)/F1_sd)
  abline(h=2)
  abline(h=-2)
  plot((F_[2,]-F2_mean)/F2_sd)
  abline(h=2)
  abline(h=-2)
  plot((F_[3,]-F3_mean)/F3_sd)
  abline(h=2)
  abline(h=-2)
   
}
```

## Look at the simplex: BAMF_F {data-background="slide_background.svg"}

Let's include the simplex as an input:

```{stan output.var='priors', eval = FALSE, tidy = FALSE}
functions {
  matrix vector_array_to_matrix(vector[] x) {
    matrix[size(x), rows(x[1])] y;
    for (m in 1:size(x))
      y[m] = x[m]';
    return y;
  }
}

data {
  int<lower=1> n;     // number of data points
  int<lower=1> m;     // number of dimensions
  int<lower=1> p;     // number of components
  matrix[n,m] X;      // data matrix
  matrix<lower=0>[n,m] sigma;  // separate sigma for each of the observations (!)
  vector<lower=0>[n-1] timesteps; //How much time elapses between values in X (arbitrary unit, but unit choice also affects other priors)
  real<lower=0> minerr; //Minimal error
  matrix<lower=0>[p,m] F; // now we use the original F as data
}

transformed data {
  vector[n*m] Xv = to_vector(X);
  vector[n*m] sigmav = to_vector(sigma);
}

parameters {
  matrix<lower=0>[n,p] G; // score matrix
  vector<lower=0>[p] alpha_a; // Posterior a
  vector<lower=minerr>[p] alpha_b; // Posterior b
}

model {

  // The priors for G and F are implicitly given in the parameters section,
  //  so explicitly stating them here would only lead to unnecessary calculations
  //  (uniform priors become additive constants (in logspace), that can be ignored).
  
  // Column-wise autocorrelation
  for(j in 1:p) {
    G[2:,j] ~ cauchy(G[:(n-1),j], alpha_a[j]*timesteps + alpha_b[j]);
  }

  // X ~ Z = G * F
  Xv ~ normal(to_vector(G*F), sigmav);

}

```

And now lets sample

```{r, echo=F, message=FALSE, warning=F, results="hide", cache=F}
file = "../models/bamf_F.stan"

mod_f <- cmdstan_model(file)
data_list <- list(n=N, m=M , p=P, X=X_, sigma=E_, timesteps=t, minerr=
    min((E_)) / 10, F=F_
)
fit_bamf_f <- mod_f$sample(
  data = data_list, 
  seed = 123, 
  chains = 4, 
  parallel_chains = 4,
  refresh = 0 # print update every 500 iters
)

```

```{r, results='hold'}
quick_diagnostic_plots_with_F(fit_bamf_f)

```

## Gaussian model with F as input: BAMF_gauss {data-background="slide_background.svg"}

We try to see how necessary is the Cauchy prior We replace the Cauchy with a Gaussian, still, with F as data

```{stan output.var='priors', eval = FALSE, tidy = FALSE}
functions {
  matrix vector_array_to_matrix(vector[] x) {
    matrix[size(x), rows(x[1])] y;
    for (m in 1:size(x))
      y[m] = x[m]';
    return y;
  }
}

data {
  int<lower=1> n;     // number of data points
  int<lower=1> m;     // number of dimensions
  int<lower=1> p;     // number of components
  matrix[n,m] X;      // data matrix
  matrix<lower=0>[n,m] sigma;  // separate sigma for each of the observations (!)
  vector<lower=0>[n-1] timesteps; //How much time elapses between values in X (arbitrary unit, but unit choice also affects other priors)
  real<lower=0> minerr; //Minimal error
  matrix<lower=0>[p,m] F; // F used as input
}

transformed data {
  vector[n*m] Xv = to_vector(X);
  vector[n*m] sigmav = to_vector(sigma);
}

parameters {
  matrix<lower=0>[n,p] G; // score matrix
  // simplex[m] F[p]; // loadings simplex
  vector<lower=0>[p] alpha_a; // Posterior a
  vector<lower=minerr>[p] alpha_b; // Posterior b
}

model {

  // The priors for G and F are implicitly given in the parameters section,
  //  so explicitly stating them here would only lead to unnecessary calculations
  //  (uniform priors become additive constants (in logspace), that can be ignored).
  
  // Column-wise autocorrelation
  for(j in 1:p) {
    G[1,j] ~ normal(0,100); // the first time point regularised
    G[2:,j] ~ normal(G[:(n-1),j], alpha_a[j]*timesteps + alpha_b[j]); // gaussian
  }

  // X ~ Z = G * F
  Xv ~ normal(to_vector(G*F), sigmav);

}


```

We then sample the model {data-background="slide_background.svg"}

```{r,results='hide', message=F, echo=F,warning=F}
file = "../models/bamf_gauss.stan"

mod_f <- cmdstan_model(file)
data_list <- list(n=N, m=M , p=P, X=X_, sigma=E_, timesteps=t, minerr=
    min((E_)) / 10, F=F_
)
fit_bamf_gauss_f <- mod_f$sample(
  data = data_list, 
  seed = 123, 
  chains = 4, 
  parallel_chains = 4,
  refresh = 0 # print update every 500 iters
)
```

```{r}
quick_diagnostic_plots_with_F(fit_bamf_gauss_f)
```


## AR(1) Model {data-background="slide_background.svg"}

The AR-1 model
```{stan output.var='priors', eval = FALSE, tidy = FALSE}
transformed data {
  vector[n*m] Xv = to_vector(X);
  vector[n*m] sigmav = to_vector(sigma);
}

parameters {
  matrix<lower=0>[n,p] G; // score matrix
  // simplex[m] F[p]; // loadings simplex
  vector[p] alpha_a; // Posterior a
  vector[p] alpha_b; // Posterior b
  real<lower=0> sigma_a[p];
}

model {

  // The priors for G and F are implicitly given in the parameters section,
  //  so explicitly stating them here would only lead to unnecessary calculations
  //  (uniform priors become additive constants (in logspace), that can be ignored).
  
  // Column-wise autocorrelation
  for(j in 1:p) {
    G[1,j] ~ normal(0,100); // the first time point regularised
    G[2:,j] ~ normal(alpha_a[j] + alpha_b[j]*G[:(n-1),j], sigma_a[j]); // gaussian
  }

  // X ~ Z = G * F
  Xv ~ normal(to_vector(G*F), sigmav);

}

```


```{r, results='hide', message=F, echo=F,warning=F,  cache=F}
file = "../models/bamf_AR1.stan"

mod_f <- cmdstan_model(file)

    min((E_)) / 10, F=F_
)
fit_bamf_ar1_f <- mod_f$sample(
  data = data_list, 
  seed = 123, 
  chains = 4, 
  parallel_chains = 4,
  refresh = 0 # print update every 500 iters
)
```

### Conclussions {data-background="slide_background.svg"}

Tha Cauchy is not necessary to capture the dynamics (at least assuming completely observed data)

## BAMF with restricted G: bamf_restrictedG {data-background="slide_background.svg"}

Jimeng suggests adding a constraint on the sum over G matrix

```{stan output.var='priors', eval = FALSE, tidy = FALSE}
functions {
  matrix vector_array_to_matrix(vector[] x) {
    matrix[size(x), rows(x[1])] y;
    for (m in 1:size(x))
      y[m] = x[m]';
    return y;
  }
  
  # limit the G value by the sum of X matrix on row, the total concentration of every measured chemical 
  # should be larger than the G value at time point t. 
  matrix get_g_max(matrix x,int n,int p) {
    matrix[n,p] y;
    for (i in 1:n)
      for (j in 1:p)
        y[i][j] = sum(x[i])*2;
    return y;
  }
  
}


data {
  int<lower=1> n;     // number of data points
  int<lower=1> m;     // number of dimensions
  int<lower=1> p;     // number of components
  matrix[n,m] X;      // data matrix
  matrix<lower=0>[n,m] sigma;  // separate sigma for each of the observations (!)
  vector<lower=0>[n-1] timesteps; //How much time elapses between values in X (arbitrary unit, but unit choice also affects other priors)
  real<lower=0> minerr; //Minimal error
  
}

transformed data {
  vector[n*m] Xv = to_vector(X);
  vector[n*m] sigmav = to_vector(sigma);
  matrix[n,p] G_max = get_g_max(X,n,p);
}

parameters {
  matrix<lower=0,upper=1>[n,p] G_raw; // raw score matrix
  simplex[m] F[p]; // loadings simplex
  vector<lower=0>[p] alpha_a; // Posterior a
  vector<lower=minerr>[p] alpha_b; // Posterior b

}

transformed parameters {
  matrix[n,p] G = (G_max) .* G_raw; // limited score matrix
}

model {

  // The priors for G and F are implicitly given in the parameters section,
  //  so explicitly stating them here would only lead to unnecessary calculations
  //  (uniform priors become additive constants (in logspace), that can be ignored).
  
  // Column-wise autocorrelation
  for(j in 1:p) {
    // G[2:,j] ~ cauchy(G[:(n-1),j], alpha_a[j]*timesteps + alpha_b[j]);
    target += cauchy_lpdf(G[2:,j] | G[:(n-1),j], alpha_a[j]*timesteps + alpha_b[j]);
  }

  // X ~ Z = G * F
  // Xv ~ normal(to_vector(G*vector_array_to_matrix(F)), sigmav);
  target += normal_lpdf(Xv | to_vector(G*vector_array_to_matrix(F)), sigmav);

}

```

We will use Jimeng proposal of a restricted G matrix 

```{r, results='hide', message=F, echo=F,warning=F}
file = "../models/bamf_restrictedG.stan"

mod_f <- cmdstan_model(file)
data_list <- list(n=N, m=M , p=P, X=X_, sigma=E_, timesteps=t, minerr=
    min((E_)) / 10
)
fit_bamf_restricted <- mod_f$sample(
  data = data_list, 
  seed = 123, 
  chains = 4, 
  parallel_chains = 4,
  refresh = 0 # print update every 500 iters
)
```

```{r}
quick_diagnostic_plots(fit_bamf_restricted)
```

## BAMF with sparsity constraints in the F matrix {data-background="slide_background.svg"}

We enforce some sparsity constraints by ways of the Dirichlet matrix (technically we use a Symmetric sparse Dirichlet prior)

```{stan output.var='priors', eval = FALSE, tidy = FALSE}

functions {
  matrix vector_array_to_matrix(vector[] x) {
    matrix[size(x), rows(x[1])] y;
    for (m in 1:size(x))
      y[m] = x[m]';
    return y;
  }
}

data {
  int<lower=1> n;     // number of data points
  int<lower=1> m;     // number of dimensions
  int<lower=1> p;     // number of components
  matrix[n,m] X;      // data matrix
  matrix<lower=0>[n,m] sigma;  // separate sigma for each of the observations (!)
  vector<lower=0>[n-1] timesteps; //How much time elapses between values in X (arbitrary unit, but unit choice also affects other priors)
  real<lower=0> minerr; //Minimal error
  vector[m] concentration;
}

transformed data {
  vector[n*m] Xv = to_vector(X);
  vector[n*m] sigmav = to_vector(sigma);
  
}

parameters {
  matrix<lower=0>[n,p] G; // score matrix
  simplex[m] F[p]; // loadings simplex
  vector<lower=0>[p] alpha_a; // Posterior a
  vector<lower=minerr>[p] alpha_b; // Posterior b
}

model {

  // The priors for G and F are implicitly given in the parameters section,
  //  so explicitly stating them here would only lead to unnecessary calculations
  //  (uniform priors become additive constants (in logspace), that can be ignored).
  
  // Column-wise autocorrelation
  for(j in 1:p) {
    F[j] ~ dirichlet(concentration); // sparsity induced by small concent.
    G[1,j] ~ normal(0,100);
    G[2:,j] ~ cauchy(G[:(n-1),j], alpha_a[j]*timesteps + alpha_b[j]);
  }

  // X ~ Z = G * F
  Xv ~ normal(to_vector(G*vector_array_to_matrix(F)), sigmav);

}

```

We sample with 0.1 concentration parameter

```{r, results='hide', message=F, echo=F,warning=F}
file = "../models/bamf_sparse.stan"

mod_f <- cmdstan_model(file)
data_list <- list(n=N, m=M , p=P, X=X_, sigma=E_, timesteps=t, minerr=
    min((E_)) / 10, concentration = 0.01*rep(1,M))
fit_bamf_sparse <- mod_f$sample(
  data = data_list, 
  seed = 123, 
  chains = 4, 
  parallel_chains = 4,
  refresh = 0 # print update every 500 iters
)
```

```{r}
quick_diagnostic_plots(fit_bamf_sparse)
```

## Let's use the varimax rotations as init {data-background="slide_background.svg"}

The MAP solutions do not seem very promising as init, we could use the latent G inferred by Varimax, but as the plot shown, they are in a different scale than the original G.

Instead I will map the inferred F by Varimax into a simplex by softmax transform, and use it to init F

```{r}
F_init = as.matrix(fa$Y)
F_init = apply(F_init,MARGIN =2, function(x){exp(x)/sum(exp(x))})
F_init = t(F_init)

inits_chain1 <- list(F=F_init )
inits_chain2 <- list(F=F_init )
inits_chain3 <- list(F=F_init )
inits_chain4 <- list(F=F_init )

corrplot(cor(t(F_),t(F_init)))
```

We see that the varimax simplex is not perfectly aligned with the original F simplex, still we will see how it behaves as starting point.

```{r}
inits_list = list(inits_chain1,inits_chain2,inits_chain3,inits_chain4)
fit_bamf_init <- mod_f$sample(
  data = data_list, 
  seed = 123, 
  chains = 4, 
  parallel_chains = 4,
  refresh = 0, # print update every 500 iters
  init=inits_list
)

```

```{r}
quick_diagnostic_plots(fit_bamf_init)

```

# Conclusions {data-background="slide_background.svg"}

-   The Cauchy prior may not be necessary to infer the time patterns.

-   There are identifiability issues. Seems like the label switching issue in mixture models, Two columns of G are sampling the same latent variable leaving one unidentified.

-   Probably a prior that disambiguates the columns of the simplex or the time profiles could alleviate this.
